instruction.text: You will listen to a discussion about sustainable cities. Listen and choose if the statements below are true or false.
instruction.sound: You will listen to a discussion about sustainable cities. Listen and choose if the statements below are true or false.

I think we all agree that our cities need to change. Our planet will not survive if we don't commit to making some fundamental changes. But in order to make a difference, we need to plan how exactly we can reach our goal. I invited you here today to discuss our strategy. Who wants to start?

atoms.a: The speaker views environmental challenges as an urgent issue.

instruction.sound: If I may begin the discussion: carbon emissions are one of our biggest problems right now, and urban areas contribute to that immensely. We need to focus on drastically lowering our emissions. Any ideas on how to approach this issue?

atoms.a: The speaker does not view carbon emissions as a priority.

wrong.text: He states that emissions are one of their biggest problems.

instruction.text: Tick the statement that best reflects the speaker's statement. Only one answer is correct.
instruction.sound: Tick the statement that best reflects the speaker's statement. Only one answer is correct.

atoms.sound: We need to move away from cars as the primary form of inner-city transport and promote public transport and fuelless alternatives much more. More trains and trams with affordable ticket prices, as well as more safe bike paths, would make personal transport much more accessible to people without cars. Affordable housing within the city is important too, so people don't need to commute every time they go to work or the supermarket, but can walk wherever they need to go.

b: ++… walkable cities and a better public transport infrastructure within cities.
… more buses than cars to reduce traffic on the streets.
… cheaper electric cars to promote fuel-free alternatives.
… car-free zones in cities to reduce emissions that damage the environment.

instruction.text: Listen and fill in the table.

instruction.sound: I completely agree. On that topic: If we redefine inner-city transport and help the citizens be less dependent on cars, we can convert some streets and parking lots into public parks. This way, we're not only creating more green spaces in the city, but also encouraging more human interaction. We spend way too much of our time inside, but that's only because there is little to do outside. This is especially true for children. Combining those parks with playgrounds will give them reasons to play outside again. ,But why stop on ground level? Buildings can be used for the same purpose. Installing community gardens on rooftops of apartment buildings allowing residents to grow their own herbs, fruits and vegetables, not only lets them take up gardening as a fulfilling hobby, but also promotes both healthy diets and self-sufficiency. They will be less reliant on imported fruits and vegetables if they can just grow them themselves. Plus, community gardens are another great way to meet new people and make connections.

atoms.b:
• encourage human ((interaction))
• combine with ((playgrounds)) for children

• promote ((healthy)) diets
• less reliance on ((imported)) fruits and vegetables

hint.text: Bei dieser Aufgabe musst du auf Details achten. Lies dir zunächst in Ruhe alle Statements durch und überlege dir, welche Begriffe eine zentrale Rolle spielen. Das hilft dir dabei, genauer hinzuhören.
hint.label: Listen for detail

atoms.sound: We also desperately need to change how we generate electricity. Most of it is still won by burning coal and natural gases, which only accelerates climate change further. The few renewable technologies we have are not enough — it is imperative we implement them on a much larger scale.Solar panels on buildings are a nice thought, but the materials used to build them are not very sustainable either. Wind turbines disturb wildlife and cannot be built within cities. However, there are some alternatives emerging, such as smaller wind turbines shaped like trees with spinning leaves. Not only do they capture the wind from any direction, but they produce less noise and blend in a lot nicer. We need to continue to improve already existing technologies to find the best possible solution.

b: Electricity is already mostly generated with sustainable sources.
The speaker proposes that more solar panels should be installed on buildings.
++He recognises that renewable energy technologies have disadvantages too.
Large wind turbines are optimal for power generation within cities.
++Green energy generation technologies need to keep being optimised.
